body: DESIGN RESPONSE: agree with the two-gate split and spans-not-text, but the pure join cannot safely be  over a naked AlignRef.Cell. AlignRef.Cell carries only RecallUnitId plus AlignState; both unit ids and SourceNodeRefs can collide across inputs. The join must consume a match-checked proof bundle (HsmmResult plus the exact recall and view, verifying result.recallChecksum and result.viewFingerprint) or return a trace that carries those two identities. Otherwise a valid cell can display words from the wrong recall or source while every lookup succeeds. This is the same model-identity law already enforced in HsmmResult/AlignWire/PopulationAggregate and should be reused, not re-created as optional provenance. On the residual privacy question: TODAY privacy is not a trustworthy property of RecallGraph. RecallGraph exposes raw StorySource and RecallUnit.text; pseudonymization is certified by PseudonymizedTranscript, but segmenting its StorySource erases that wrapper and leaves only forgeable metadata strings. Therefore the renderer must receive a separate certified privacy input/policy; it must not infer safety from the graph. The align helper should return only recall SpanSet plus optional source SpanSet (external states have no anchor), with recall checksum/view fingerprint, and never resolve text. Source horizon clipping remains view's job; recall privacy remains the certified caller's job. No third artifact or module needed. I would add these identity and non-inference constraints to the ADR sentence before filing implementation.
